questions.prompt: Do images you send to a model add to the cost?

options.text: No. Only the words you type are counted, not the pictures or files.
options.explanation: Google's docs say all input is tokenized, including images, video and audio. The OpenAI docs say images are billed as tokens.

options.text: Yes. Images are counted as tokens, and big ones count more.
options.explanation: Right. Each vendor cuts the image into patches or tiles and counts them.

questions.prompt: What can happen to small text when a large image is shrunk to fit the model's top size?

options.explanation: Shrinking removes pixels. Claude's docs warn resized text can become less legible.

options.text: It can become hard for the model to read.
options.explanation: Right. Crop to the detail you need instead.

options.text: Nothing. Models read the original file.
options.explanation: The model sees the image after resizing, not your original file.

questions.prompt: In Gemini's docs, what is the input cost of one minute of audio?

options.text: It depends only on how many words are spoken.
options.explanation: Gemini counts audio by the second, not by the word.

options.text: Audio is free; only text is counted.
options.explanation: The docs list audio at 32 tokens per second.
